mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille required for domestic BC agent consent

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all General Partners, Limited Partners, and Beneficial Owners against OFAC (SDN List), United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, Canadian sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act (SEMA) and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Law), and the FINTRAC list of designated persons; enhanced due diligence required for any Politically Exposed Person (domestic, foreign, or international organization PEP) as defined under PCMLTFA s. 9.3 and associated FINTRAC guidance; mandatory beneficial ownership disclosure to the BC Registry for entities; ongoing risk-based monitoring; screening must be completed within 24 hours prior to registration filing and recorded in a compliance log.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_registry_obligation: British Columbia requires every registered entity, including Limited Partnerships, to maintain a register of individuals with significant control under the BC Business Corporations Act and the BC Beneficial Ownership Transparency Act, SBC 2023, c. 22; the registry must be filed annually with the BC Registrar of Companies; failure to file is a strict liability offence with significant penalties.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Corporate Registry via BC Online (https://www.bconline.gov.bc.ca) and the BC Registry Services Online portal (OneStop Business Registry - https://onestop.gov.bc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Business names must be in English or French exclusively; BC does not mandate bilingual names for provincial LPs; names in Chinese characters or other non-Roman scripts are not permitted as the legal registered name; a transliterated English/French version is mandatory; the name must not be identical, or confusingly similar, to any other registered BC company, extraprovincial entity, registered partnership, or trademark; use of the word 'Limited' or 'LP' designation to indicate limited liability status is mandatory in the full legal name; as of 2024 amendments, the term 'Limited' or 'Ltée' may be used alternatively with the abbreviation 'LP'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must submit a written appeal or request for review to the BC Registrar of Companies within 30 days of the rejection notice via BC Online or by registered mail to the Registrar, Ministry of Finance, Corporate Registry, PO Box 9431 Stn Prov Govt, Victoria, BC V8W 9V3. The applicant may file a corporate name approval request (body corporate name request) with NUANS-style search results and provide evidence of sufficient distinction. If the Registrar upholds the rejection, the applicant may apply for judicial review to the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, RSBC 1996, c. 241. For healthcare-related terms such as 'Health Fitness', a confirmation of exemption or a signed statutory declaration from a registered medical professional may be required; otherwise the proposed name must be resubmitted with a distinct mark.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.statutory_reference: Under the British Columbia Partnership Act, RSBC 1996, c. 348, s. 6 and the Partnership Regulation, a Limited Partnership must maintain a registered office in British Columbia at all times.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for the registered office address only if a physical street address in British Columbia is provided, mail forwarding is arranged, and the address is capable of receiving legal service of process; the BC Registry does not permit a private mailbox (e.g., a commercial mailbox from a postal provider) as a registered office; however, in practice, a licensed registered agent's physical office address is widely used and constitutes an acceptable commercial substance proxy for a pure digital health app business with no physical stock, no employees in BC, and no physical operations in BC.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approx. 2-4% probability) for a pass-through Limited Partnership engaged exclusively in digital SaaS/biometric telemetry with no physical premises, no employees in BC, and no tax registration requirement beyond the LP registration. The Corporate Registry is not a revenue enforcement agency and does not conduct physical inspections for LPs except in specific enforcement scenarios involving fraud, money laundering, or tax evasion; the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) or the BC Ministry of Finance may conduct a desk audit with a probable physical inspection risk of approximately 1% annually for low-risk digital enterprises; however, under the FINTRAC client identification and record-keeping regime (PCMLTFA), any reporting entity processing IAP/Google Play payments with a Canadian nexus is subject to unscheduled compliance examinations, which may include requests for beneficial ownership documentation and business records.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.commercial_substance_recommendations: The LP should maintain a physical address via the registered office agent, retain all financial and alternative payment records for at least 6 years (Income Tax Act s. 230), and ensure that at least one general partner is resident in Canada or appoint a BC-resident attorney for service if all partners are non-resident; maintaining a British Columbia mobile app developer license is not required because no statutory license is triggered under ISIC 6201.

stage_1.jurisdictional_note: British Columbia Limited Partnerships are pass-through vehicles for Canadian federal income tax purposes under the Income Tax Act, RSC 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.); the LP itself is not a taxpayer. The general partner is jointly and severally liable for the obligations of the LP in the absence of an incorporated general partner; all partners (general and limited) are jointly and severally liable for debts and obligations of the LP to the extent provided by the Partnership Act; limited partners may lose limited liability by participating in the control of the business of the LP. For a digital health app with IAP and Google Play Billing, the LP should also comply with PIPEDA (Canada's federal private-sector privacy law, as of September 2024, Part 1 replaced by the Consumer Privacy Protection Act via Bill C-27 not yet fully proclaimed) and BC's Personal Information Protection Act, SBC 2003, c. 63 if collecting BC resident health data; a privacy impact assessment is strongly recommended.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal income tax and British Columbia Ministry of Finance for provincial tax administration
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities: Submit Business Number application via CRA My Account portal; Canadian Limited Partnerships: Obtain Business Number from CRA and register for GST/HST if taxable supplies exceed threshold
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election; Canadian partnership taxation rules apply with potential GAAR for hybrid mismatches

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic filing of GST/HST returns via CRA My Business Account; real-time fiscal data reporting and digital clearance requirements

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Canada or services supplied to non-residents, including digital health apps to offshore users, qualify for 0% GST/HST rate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA conducts audits for export substantiation; penalties up to 50% of tax or criminal sanctions for fraudulent claims; retrospective clawback of zero-rated amounts if documentation inadequate

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada, operating in concert with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential supervision, the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for AML oversight, and the Department of Finance for exchange-control policy formulation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains unrestricted current-account and capital-account convertibility under IMF Article VIII. There is no Exchange Control Act or statutory foreign-exchange licensing regime; both capital injections and profit repatriation are freely permitted. For a British Columbia limited partnership with non-resident partners, distributions are subject to Part XIII withholding tax unless reduced by an applicable income tax treaty, and Form NR4 must be filed. Convertibility and transfers do not require Bank of Canada approval, but cross-border wire transfers over C$10,000 must be reported by the receiving financial institution to FINTRAC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Canada imposes no export-proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no statutory timeline for conversion of foreign-currency export receipts. Digital app subscription revenue earned via Apple IAP and Google Play Billing may be retained in USD or other foreign currency, converted at commercial rates, or kept in multi-currency treasury accounts without prior regulatory authorization. Standard CRA reporting for income and GST/HST remains the only compliance obligation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Corporate Settlement Account
Operational Account with Non-Resident Owner Wire Integration
Settlement and Payables Account with Commercial LC Facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium. Canada does not grant foreign electronic money institutions (EMIs) bank status or the ability to take unrestricted deposits. An offshore EMI may operate as a money-services business (MSB) registered with FINTRAC and offer payment-clearing services, but it cannot provide regulated deposit services, escrow, or lending products. For this BC LP, an offshore EMI is viable only as a supplementary disbursement or payout engine; the primary treasury relationship and clearing infrastructure must remain anchored with an OSFI-regulated Schedule I bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is recognized in Canada under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. For a BC limited partnership, the general partner or a designated senior officer must complete identity verification via video conference or through an approved (often notarized) attestation process. Physical branch attendance is not an absolute statutory mandate, but several Schedule I banks nevertheless require at least one in-person, verifiable interview for non-resident-controlled partnerships; remote video verification is increasingly accepted when accompanied by certified corporate records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: LP beneficial-ownership complexity caused by undisclosed or layered partnership interests.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered LP statement from the BC Registrar, definitive partnership agreement, sworn partner schedule identifying every direct and indirect partner, certified KYC package for the general partner, and a signed organizational chart showing the ultimate beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-wealth ambiguity for a large cross-border capital injection from offshore contributors to the LP.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank reference letters, audited financial statements or certified accounting records, tax filings from the transferring entity, a notarized source-of-funds declaration, and underlying transactional evidence such as a sale agreement, dividend warrant, or promissory note tied to the exact remitting bank account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border revenue flow from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing raising royalty or licensing uncertainty.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apple Developer Program Agreement and Google Play Developer Distribution Agreement, App Store Connect and Google Play Console financial reports, an intercompany license/royalty agreement (if IP is licensed from a related entity), a functional-language accounting mapping for revenue recognition, and a valid Canadian GST/HST registration certificate.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections must arrive by SWIFT MT103 or Fedwire in US dollars (or the appropriate CAD settlement rail) into the BC LP's Schedule I bank treasury account. Wire instructions must reference the LP's legal name, Canadian Business Number, and an alphanumeric capital-call reference. The receiving bank should be supplied with the following for routing and FINTRAC due diligence: the capital contribution statement, the limited partnership certificate, a board or general-partner resolution approving the capital call, and the underlying subscription agreement. Purpose codes should identify the transfer as investment/capital, such as the SWIFT purpose code 'INVS' (investment) or 'CAPT' (capital transfer), consistent with the bank's fixed wire-transfer formats. For any single inbound transfer equal to or exceeding C$10,000, the bank files an electronic funds transfer report with FINTRAC.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements should be executed via SWIFT MT103 for B2B vendor payments and cross-border supplier settlements, with the corresponding invoice number in the payment reference field. For high-value physical merchandise or contracted deliverables, a commercial letter of credit issued under UCP600 provides secure settlement through the BC LP's account bank. Canadian-dollar disbursements can clear through Payments Canada (ACSS or the high-value LVTS, with migration to the Real-Time Rail), while US-dollar disbursements use CHIPS or SWIFT USD clearing. Each outgoing payment must be reconciled to the underlying trade invoice, the hedged FX ticket, and the relevant GST/HST or customs documentation when applicable.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Currency forwards (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, CAD/GBP) on standard tenors of 1, 3, 6, and 12 months
FX swaps and rollover swaps for cash-flow management of cross-border working capital
Commercial cross-currency interest rate swaps for long-term partnership financing or intercompany loan hedging
Offshore NDF contracts on non-convertible currencies (e.g., local Asia/EM currencies) available through Canadian bank global trading desks, provided ISDA/CSA documentation is in place
OTC vanilla FX options with collateral arrangements and clear ISDA master agreements for treasury hedging of subscription and subscription-related vendor flows

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, BC Corporate Registry, Province of British Columbia
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 60 days after the anniversary date of the limited partnership's registration in British Columbia; a December 31 fiscal year-end does not change this anniversary-based deadline.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by the statutory deadline places the limited partnership in default status. The Registrar may refuse to issue certificates or status letters, impose late filing and reinstatement fees, and, after continued default, administratively dissolve or cancel the limited partnership's registration. Reinstatement requires payment of all arrears and a restoration filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return and T5013 Summary (where a filing obligation applies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency, Partnership Information Return Program
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The T5013 return and summary are due no later than five months after the limited partnership's fiscal period end; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the filing deadline is May 31. Partner T5013 statements must generally be furnished by the CRA-prescribed issue date, normally March 31 for calendar-year partnerships.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts administrative penalties calculated under the Income Tax Act based on the number of partners and reportable amounts. Continued or deliberate failure may result in higher penalties, gross-negligence penalties, or prosecution. Late filing does not cause registry strike-off but may impair the limited partnership's CRA compliance status.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A BC limited partnership has no general statutory audit requirement under the Limited Partnership Act. A compulsory independent audit is triggered when the limited partnership is a reporting issuer under Canadian securities legislation, when a sectoral regulator or health-data certification authority requires an attestation, when the partnership agreement or a lender mandates audited financial statements, or when an applicable Canadian tax or securities framework imposes audit-based accountability.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS if the limited partnership is a publicly accountable enterprise or is required by Canadian securities regulators; Canadian ASPE, Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook, if the limited partnership is a private entity and not required to use IFRS. Financial statements used for partner allocations and Canadian tax reporting should reconcile to the chosen accounting framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: British Columbia does not require a separate public UBO annual filing for limited partnerships. The LP must maintain a current register of limited partners showing names, addresses, contributions, profit shares, and transfer dates; any transfer of a limited partnership interest must be entered in the register before the next annual report. Before filing the annual report, the general partner must reconcile the partner register and significant control records against the annual report and retain a dated annual confirmation in the minute book. This internal reconciliation serves as the annual UBO verification; no separate UBO return is submitted to the BC Registrar.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (limited partners register with contributions, profit shares, and transfers)
Register of Directors (for a corporate general partner; otherwise the general partner's management authority records)
Minute Book (partnership resolutions, partner consents, and annual confirmations)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $200 - $450 (typical BC registered office and registered agent retainer)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: No statutory audit fee applies absent an external requirement; a voluntary or regulator-required audit of a small digital-health LP typically ranges from $6,000 to $18,000 USD, while an unaudited compilation or review ranges from $2,500 to $6,500 USD.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Combined federal and British Columbia headline corporate income tax rate of 27% (15% federal general rate plus 12% BC general corporate rate). The BC limited partnership itself is fiscally transparent; each corporate partner will be subject to corporate rates on its allocated share, while individual partners are taxed at personal progressive rates (top combined BC marginal rate approximately 53.5%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No broad statutory tax holiday exists in Canada. A Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) may claim the federal small business deduction on active business income up to CA$500,000, yielding an approximate 11% combined federal/BC rate for eligible CCPC partners. Refundable federal Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credits are available for eligible software development, including health-fitness app R&D, at 35% for CCPCs on qualifying expenditures up to CA$3,000,000, with a provincial BC R&D tax credit for eligible expenditures.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 Partnership Information Return (federal and BC provincial schedules), filed electronically through the CRA EFILE/NETFILE portal or via a registered agent using My Business Account; BC provincial allocation is embedded in the T5013 and remitted through the BC Corporate Online service where applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T5013 return must be filed on or before the later of March 31 following the calendar year in which the fiscal period ends and five months after the end of the partnership fiscal period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 1 - Partnership Identification and Partner Allocations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Trade name, CRA business number, BC limited partnership registration number, address of principal place of business, fiscal year-end, and complete allocation of income/loss to each limited and general partner in accordance with the partnership agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List non-resident partners with full foreign tax identification numbers and country of residence. For allocations to non-resident partners, apply the ITA s.103 forced-allocation rules where the partnership agreement has been manipulated to disproportionately benefit non-residents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Revenue Schedule (Box 20 – Business Revenue and Related Amounts)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from subscription fees, Apple IAP, Google Play Billing, advertising, and licensing, net of platform transaction commissions, for the fitness biometric tracking and wellness telemetry app.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Canadian-source and treaty-allocable business revenue; ensure that international revenue is excluded where the LP has no permanent establishment under the relevant DTA allocation provisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of partnership income to British Columbia using the permanent establishment and BC-source apportionment formula, including payroll, gross revenue, and IP exploitation location.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the LP carries on business with a permanent establishment outside BC, the BC allocation must be reduced accordingly; non-resident partners should obtain a written position substantiating source-country allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 8 – Foreign Income and Foreign Tax Credit Reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of foreign-source app income, foreign taxes paid on that income, and restated partnership income for Canadian tax purposes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners cannot claim Canadian foreign tax credits for foreign taxes; they should tile through their domestic credit mechanism. Resident partners claiming a foreign tax credit must attach supporting treaty or non-treaty documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of amounts paid or credited to non-resident partners constituting Part XIII taxable allocated income, including deemed dividends, interest, royalties, and active business income allocated from a Canadian PE.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Submit an NR301 waiver or comparable treaty relief before remittance where a treaty reduces withholding; no relief is available for an allocation exceeding the partner's capital contribution unless supported by at-risk economic substance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: CRA may impose a daily penalty of CA$100 per late T5013 return or slip, up to CA$2,500 per slip, plus separate penalties for false statements equal to 50% of the understated tax and arrears interest compounded daily at prescribed rates. Failure to remit Part XIII WHT exposes a 10% penalty under ITA s.227 plus interest on the unremitted amount.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% statutory Part XIII withholding tax on Canadian-source income allocated to a non-resident partner, including income flowing from the fitness app partnership. Where a corporate partner owns at least 10% of the votes of the recipient payer and a DTA applies, the treaty rate is 5%; for portfolio distributions the treaty rate is 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident partner must annually provide to the LP: (i) a valid certificate of residence / tax residency certificate issued by the partner's tax authority; (ii) a completed NR301 waiver request where the payment is a pre-agreed allocation; and (iii) a written confirmation of beneficial ownership and absence of a permanent establishment in Canada. The LP must file the waivers with CRA and remit the reduced withholding to the Receiver General of Canada. Retroactive relief may be obtained by filing an amended T3016/NR7 refund package and CRA's NPR-AMR procedure before the due date of the relevant assessment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate for royalties and interest paid to non-residents is 25% Part XIII WH. Treaties may reduce royalties to as low as 10% (Canada–US DTA applies 10% to software and industrial royalties); arm's-length interest is frequently reduced to 0% under the Canada–US treaty and 10% in many non-US DTAs; related-party interest requires a debt ratio and arm's-length rate analysis.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: For Canada, a Local File and contemporaneous transfer-pricing study is expected where aggregate non-arm's-length cross-border transactions of the LP exceed CA$1,000,000 in the fiscal year. A Master File and Country-by-Country Report are mandatory for members of an MNE group with consolidated group revenue of CA$750,000,000 or more. Transactions between the LP and a related foreign IP-holding entity should be supported by a benchmarked arm's-length pricing analysis.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not implement Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations; instead, substance is tested through ITA s.247 transfer-pricing rules, the general anti-avoidance rule in s.245, the 'sham' doctrine, and the 'brass-arrow' and limited-partner control rules. For a BC limited partnership, limited partners lose liability insulation if they participate in control of the business; the LP must also maintain real premises, employees, books, and contractual decision-making in BC to resist treaty-shopping and substance-based assessments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to report sub-sources of fitness app revenue (Apple IAP, Google Play subscriptions, advertising, and telemetry data sales), deliberately understating Canadian-source income, shifting revenue to an offshore conduit, or falsifying T5013 returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Indictable conviction under Income Tax Act s.239(1) exposing a fine of 50% to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to five years; CRA may also impose gross negligence penalties of 50% of the understated tax plus compound arrears interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the general partner may be assessed jointly and severally under ITA s.227.1 for unremitted withholding; civil restitution may attach to personal assets; conviction will cause criminal record, restrictions on serving as a director, potential detention under the Criminal Code, and, for proven flight risk, a Canadian travel ban under s.225.2 departure order.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing a foreign IP-holding entity in a zero-rate territory with no personnel, no economic decision-making, and no active management, to receive license fees or capital gain from the LP while the substantive R&D and app development remain in BC; using deferred revenue agreements to inflate foreign profits without compensating BC employees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA will apply s.247 to reallocate profits, s.245 GAAR to disregard the arrangement, and reassess with late-filing penalties; under the OECD multilateral instrument, such a hybrid or shell arrangement may be denied treaty benefits, resulting in full 25% Part XIII withholding on payments historically treated as exempt.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who design or approve artificial arrangements face personal assessments for negligent planning under the Canadian common-law duty; a BC court may pierce the LP veil, rendering general partners and controlling directors jointly liable for full corporate and tax debts, and may order a non-resident director's equitable compensation under cross-border arbitration letters.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / FINTRAC Reporting Breach for Digital Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting Apple IAP and Google Play payments without registering as a money services business, failing to maintain transaction records over FINTRAC thresholds, or using crypto and unreported e-wallet rails to avoid total gross revenue disclosure; structuring transactions to remain below the CAS$10,000 reporting threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act of up to CA$500,000 for an individual and CA$1,000,000 for a partnership, plus criminal fines or imprisonment for money laundering under the Criminal Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of an unregistered MSB face personal liability for unreported capital gains when proceeds are traced; an inability to produce records can lead to an initial injunction freezing the partnership's bank accounts and personal bank accounts of directors under the Criminal Code proceeds-of-crime provisions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Licensing of the fitness app's patented tracking algorithm or user data to a related foreign entity at a below-arm's-length price while the BC partnership bears all employee, server, and legal costs; entering a cost-sharing arrangement that strips Canadian residual profit to an offshore principal.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA reassessment under s.247(2)/(3) adds the transaction adjustment to income; a penalty under s.247(3) equals 10% of the adjustment for failing to make a reasonable effort to determine arm's-length price; in aggravated cases, s.163(2) negligence penalties of 50% of understated tax apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the LP's general partner may be sued in civil courts for knowing participation in a s.247 arrangement; if the LP becomes insolvent because of the reassessment, the directors can be held personally liable for unpaid employee source withholdings and unremitted royalties through the Crown's priority charge over partnership assets.
